verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew successfully splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Floating in the Pacific Ocean... waters off San Diego'; R2: 'splashed down in the Pacific Ocean, about 40 to 50 miles off the coast of San Diego'; R3: 'splashed down off the coast of San Diego'; R4: 'splashed down into the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego'; R5: 'splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego'; R6: 'safely splashed down at 8:07 p.m. ET... off the coast of San Diego'
verifications.reasoning: All references directly state the splashdown location as Pacific Ocean off San Diego, California, with successful recovery.

verifications.claim: The Orion capsule landed on April 10, 2026, at 8:07 p.m. ET (5:07 p.m. PT).
verifications.label: CLEAR

verifications.claim: The Orion capsule landed following a 10-day mission around the moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'mission began on April 1... splashdown on Friday (April 10)'; R2: 'historic 10-day trip to the moon'; R3: 'After 10 days and 695,000 miles'; R4: 'officially 10-day mission... around the moon'; R5: 'ending historic 10-day mission to the moon'; R6: 'record-breaking 10-day mission... around the moon'
verifications.reasoning: All references describe it as a 10-day mission (launch April 1 to splashdown April 10) involving a flyby around the moon.

verifications.claim: The mission goal was finalizing the first crewed trip to the moon in over 50 years.
verifications.label: CLEAR

verifications.reasoning: All references confirm it as the first crewed lunar mission since 1972 (over 50 years), with goals of testing systems for future trips, successfully completed.
